summary: A summary from the Network Information Center's viewpoint of what was decided at the February 23, 1973 Network Mail Meeting at SRI-ARC. The main outcome was adding a new FTP mail command with fields such as TO, FROM, AUTHOR and TITLE, where recipients use a user@host form. It points to RFC 475 for a fuller summary.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC summarizes decisions from a meeting about network mail. It describes proposed message fields and the NIC's role in addressing and recording mail.

subtitle: The NIC's summary of conclusions from the Network Mail meeting.

sections.title: The Network Mail Meeting
sections.content: Michael Kudlick summarizes the principal conclusions of the Network Mail Meeting held at SRI-ARC on February 23, 1973. He says this NIC viewpoint has no major disagreement with a more comprehensive summary and refers readers to related RFCs for background and further detail.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC gives the NIC's short account of a network mail meeting. The author directs readers to other documents for more complete coverage.

sections.title: Fields for Network Mail
sections.content:
The meeting called for additional FTP mail requirements in a new mail command. Proposed subcommands include TO, FROM, AUTHOR, TITLE, ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, RECORDED, and TYPE, as well as TEXT, FILE, and CITATION.

The TO field allows multiple addresses in the form user@host. FROM identifies the sender and provides a return address for undeliverable mail; AUTHOR can name multiple authors.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposed command has fields for recipients, sender, authors, and title. Other fields describe delivery notices, recording, message type, and whether the message contains text or a citation.

sections.title: Addressing, Delivery, and Recording
sections.content:
The report describes the NIC as a possible directory for translating user identifications into standard user@host addresses, and as an intermediate point for mail that should be recorded or forwarded. It distinguishes delivery to a recipient's host from the recipient actually reading the message.

Recorded mail would receive a NIC accession number for later reference. The report also discusses optional delivery acknowledgements, recipient storage choices, and citations that point readers to a file instead of sending its contents.
sections.plainLanguage: The NIC could help map a person's identification to an address and keep a record of selected mail. An acknowledgement would show delivery to a host, not that the person had read the mail.
